events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $4.41 (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip, so the fare is metered and extra distance enters the fare; the refund formula is Σ(extra_km of un-exempt segments) × the trip's per-km rate, taken as distance fare ÷ distance km ($31.84 ÷ 22.58 km = $1.4101/km) [F5][F7][RD-2]. Two off-route segments are on the record: F3 (2.69 km extra) and F4 (3.13 km extra) [F3][F4][RD-1].

Segment F3 (21:42–21:49) is exempt: an LTA-reported accident on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route, was reported at 21:26 — before the segment began and inside the trip window — matching the driver's account that blocked lanes forced the diversion [F12][F9][RD-4(a)].

Segment F4 (22:02–22:09) is not exempt. The only traffic records for its window are speed bands (PIE band 5, KPLY band 4), and a speed band alone does not exempt a segment under RD-4(b) [F10][F11][RD-4]. No rider consent exists: there is a complete chat record with no messages at all, so no rider message before 22:02:05 agrees to anything, and the driver's post-trip statement that the extra distance "was unavoidable" is a claim, not rider consent, and names the KPLY rather than the second stretch [F8][F9][RD-5][G11]. No rider-requested stop was recorded to bring this segment within RD-3 [RD-3].

Amount: 3.13 km × $1.4101/km = $4.4136, rounded to $4.41 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The rest of the $9.45 excess-distance charge, including the F3 stretch, is not refunded.

Account action: the driver's 90-day profile shows 1 upheld dispute but 0 upheld route disputes, so the RD-6 repeated-breach threshold (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no flag_account is added; the profile facts are not used to decide the deviation itself [F14][F15][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the (empty) chat record and the driver's statement — the complaint is about route and fare only, the statement explains a diversion, and no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so the screen is "none" [F8][F9].

Evidence: the record settles every element used — measured segments with extra_km, the matching incident report and timing, the complete chat record and the fare breakdown — so evidence_status is "sufficient" [F3][F4][F5][F7][F8][F12].

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F4] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 22:02:05 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “There was an accident on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway ahead, lanes were blocked, so I went round it. The extra distance was unavoidable.” (F9)
